What was chosen. What was actually said.

The visible faces of these 20 records are the complete reading layer. Open a record for the same decision's mechanism, exact wording, and source witnesses.

A test establishes what was specified; it does not manufacture a reason. “Unexplained” identifies a gap in the inspected record, not a judgment about the choice. Tests below are source evidence; the symnav suite was not run for this page.

01
The caller had not moved yet

Package ownership was staged; production invocation was left for the next review boundary.

01
REASON STATED
Keep the shipped CLI on its compatibility graph

Stage the package mechanisms, but leave the CLI dispatcher on app-local imports. Freeze 38 production copies with a path-and-source SHA-256 digest; normalize CRLF to LF. The three host-routing files are outside that freeze.

WHY RECORDED

Mechanism ownership and host invocation coordination need separate review boundaries.

Open the record
↗
02
REASON STATED
Put real mechanisms and executable entries inside the package

Group client, registry, transport, execution, delivery, process, worker, lifecycle, resources, and diagnostics under @symnav/daemon. Launch package-relative process and worker entries with no named exports. Copy the spool record codec into delivery so it no longer imports CLI output code; keep zero dependencies on other internal production packages.

WHY RECORDED

Give daemon policy and mechanism one home with an enforced boundary.

Open the record
↗
03
REASON UNEXPLAINED
Retire the temporary policy-testing export and its checks

Remove @symnav/daemon/policy-testing. Put override factories in CLI/package test helpers; update imports and lock exact root + process-entry + worker-entry exports. Delete the special lint restriction, its two lint tests, and the temporary-subpath export/declaration tests.

WHY RECORDED

No separate rationale for this export retirement and the associated test deletions was found in the PR body, commit bodies, or supplied plans.

Open the record
↗
02
The client owns the consequences of a route

Keep the order, the independent warm-up, the replay boundary, and the output owner together.

04
REASON STATED
Keep the public façade free of Node ambient types

Expose DaemonClient.execute/control and portable contracts. Dynamically import its private Node runtime through a string-typed module URL; loading begins in the constructor, and each method awaits the same runtime promise. This is a declaration boundary, not browser execution support.

WHY RECORDED

Host declarations must not acquire Node ambient dependencies.

Open the record
↗
05
REASON STATED
The first routing decision stops later observation

Disabled execution bypasses registry routing. Otherwise evaluate record present → not starting → version compatible → responsive, in that order. Read/observe lazily and memoize each operation. Missing, starting, recovering, dead, incompatible, and warm routes keep their distinct effects; only confirmed exit asks routing to remove the record.

WHY RECORDED

The first routing decision must prevent every later side effect.

Open the record
↗
06
REASON STATED
Answer locally without waiting for warm-up

Cold/fallback attempts create a fresh host executor. Absent records and fallback routes trigger startup independently; starting/recovering routes do not. Swallow background trigger failures, preserve the chosen route, forward argv/cwd/telemetry, and give local executors a no-op resource sampler.

WHY RECORDED

Ordinary commands must answer locally while a daemon warms; a daemon becoming ready must not cancel or duplicate local work.

Open the record
↗
07
REASON STATED
Replay warm work only when transport says it is safe

Use the existing DaemonTransportError.retrySafe authority for one local fallback. Uncertain submission, accepted-work failure, non-retry-safe rejection, and malformed/failed completion stay warm and return a controlled failure; they do not replay locally or invalidate ownership through this client path.

WHY RECORDED

Timeout or disconnect is not evidence that a healthy daemon or accepted work can be discarded.

Open the record
↗
08
REASON STATED
Own warm output capture and controlled failure bytes

Create fresh result captures in the OS temporary directory from output policy; the public host supplies no storage/output factory. Package-private transport accepts an internal capture factory. Map resource/response/other failures to three stderr messages with exit code 1; malformed exit codes or missing output become controlled warm failures, disposing available malformed output.

WHY RECORDED

Warm transfer cleanup and replay safety belong to the daemon client.

Open the record
↗
09
REASON STATED
The host supplies product knowledge, including the readiness probe

Options require state directory, product version, enabled flag, executor factory/module URL, and readiness probe; policy is optional. Execute receives workspace root, command name, argv, cwd, and telemetry. Forward the host's readiness command/argv through startup with telemetry off and legacy cold mode; the internal coordinator retains a --version default.

WHY RECORDED

The daemon must run commands without knowing what they are; CLI syntax stays in the host.

Open the record
↗
10
REASON UNEXPLAINED
Keep lifecycle composition inside the client

Reuse composed controllers and a startup coordinator. Give status its own response timeout/transport, keep start and stop on the routing transport, and let mechanism errors reject for a host wrapper. Typed overloads return one action's report. Disabled blocks start, while status and stop remain callable.

WHY RECORDED

The host-facing control boundary is specified; no separate reason was found for this exact controller/timeout composition or the disabled-control asymmetry.

Open the record
↗
03
Identity and time have named owners

The extraction also narrowed construction, centralized startup equality, and preserved the old lifetime behavior.

11
REASON UNEXPLAINED
Validate process coordinates before composing its internals

Rename WorkspaceDaemon to DaemonProcessCoordinator. Replace loose identity fields with supplied coordinates validated against workspace root/keys/endpoint at constructor entry; adopt that endpoint. Require a DaemonClock, rename transport to a serving-only server, narrow filesystem injection to workspaceExists, and characterize cyclic callbacks as bound but not invoked during construction.

WHY RECORDED

The architecture requests a process coordinator; the commits specify these construction choices without recording why this exact contract was chosen.

Open the record
↗
12
REASON UNEXPLAINED
Preserve the request-specific authentication order

Add characterization around the existing process request dispatcher: identify/terminate/kill use their credential paths before the general protocol/instance gate; ping uses that gate; execute checks its token before admission observations; execution-status/result-fetch/result-ack validate tokens before ledger or delivery access. The remaining stop path drains accepted work and waits for acknowledgements.

WHY RECORDED

The PR adds order-sensitive tests and adopts the new coordinate fields; no rationale for the inherited request-by-request authentication asymmetry was found.

Open the record
↗
13
REASON UNEXPLAINED
Ask the registry which startup owner still matches

Centralize startup-owner equality in the registry and replace caller comparisons with named operations. Match identity+instance always, credentials/kind/PID only when required, and full acquiredAt/heartbeatAt/revision snapshots for owner-sensitive mutations. Preserve guarded writes, ownership rereads, launcher handoff, and cleanup against changed owners.

WHY RECORDED

A single lock-ownership authority is requested in the architecture spec. No separate rationale for the narrow-versus-full comparison choices was found.

Open the record
↗
14
REASON STATED
Daemon time comes through DaemonClock

Remove the lifetime's telemetry Clock dependency and scattered time callbacks. Use wallNowMs for lifetime, ledger timestamps, registry leases, controller/termination deadlines, and replacement windows; use monotonicNowMs for queue/activity and worker durations. The process injects one clock into its composed owners; NodeDaemonClock owns the two real sources.

WHY RECORDED

The architecture gives the daemon its own wall and monotonic clock instead of using telemetry as shared utilities.

Open the record
↗
15
REASON STATED
Do not remember the deferred idle changes as shipped

Keep the constructor-started, navigation-acceptance-reset idle deadline. Completion only marks the queue idle; if the deadline has passed, idle shutdown can begin then. Record readiness-armed and completion-based idle intervals as two future behavior changes, leaving the interval itself unchanged.

WHY RECORDED

Readiness- and completion-based lifetime changes are explicitly deferred behavior.

Open the record
↗
04
The evidence moved, and some of it changed

37 mechanism test files moved. The deletions, narrower checks, platform branch, and test configuration are decisions too.

16
REASON STATED
Move mechanism tests to their package owner

Move 37 app-local mechanism test files into daemon source directories, with package-local helpers and generic executor fixtures. Keep CLI integration/e2e ownership in the app; the changed e2e expectations are unchanged apart from helper imports/names. Add façade, routing, contract, boundary, registry, construction, and built-entry characterization.

WHY RECORDED

The extraction spec directs tests that reach into daemon internals to use the public surface or move into the package.

Open the record
↗
17
REASON UNEXPLAINED
Delete the mocked CLI entry tests; add package entry evidence

Delete daemon-entry.test.ts and its two app-local cases: configuration/logger/termination-observer wiring and source independence. Add package production/entry boundary checks and real built worker, launcher, and process-entry tests for configuration, one initialization, missing modules/exports, and ownership cleanup. They exercise different boundaries.

WHY RECORDED

The commits name the retirement and the built-entry proofs, but no reason is recorded for discarding those exact mock-level observations or treating the replacement evidence as sufficient.

Open the record
↗
18
REASON UNEXPLAINED
The moved worker test no longer exercises the same CLI integration

Replace the injected CLI readiness scenario with a generic executor; remove its discovery/indexing/total duration expectations. Delete the worker-level CLI version-mismatch initialization-failure test; restore version rejection as a direct CLI executor-factory test. Generic module failures remain tested, but the old combined CLI-worker path is no longer that test.

WHY RECORDED

Package independence is a stated extraction constraint. No reason was found for the loss of the duration assertions or for replacing that worker-level rejection observation with a factory-level one.

Open the record
↗
19
REASON UNEXPLAINED
Windows termination has a different cleanup witness

The new built-process test branches on win32: after termination it expects the ready record to remain and no process-termination diagnostic, then the test harness removes the exited process record. Other platforms expect self-cleanup and that diagnostic. Both branches finally assert no record or owner.

WHY RECORDED

The final commit specifies the platform branch. It provides no body explaining the OS-level reason or why this is the chosen observation.

↗

REASON UNEXPLAINED
Make daemon test files run serially and add tsx

Add a daemon-specific Vitest configuration with fileParallelism: false, and add tsx ^4.21.0 as a daemon dev dependency with a lockfile update. This changes the test execution setup alongside the extraction.

WHY RECORDED

No reason for disabling test-file parallelism or for the exact new dev-dependency choice was found in the PR body, commit bodies, or supplied plans.
